Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC task 6f799da8 — evidence/notes for future related tasks

This instance ended at attempt cap (8 wrong; 8 demos). All demos used two colors (foreground + background) and output recolors selected cells to color 1. Test was 28x22 with 4-color foreground and 9 background; nonblank figure rows 6–9 and 21–24, with large all-9 separators. No solution was found. Do not treat the speculative hypotheses below as a confirmed rule.

## Most reliable observations from demonstrations

- Demo 7 (13x15, colors 0/8): three isolated 1-row horizontal bars at r3 (8s c0–2), r7 (8s c0–14), r11 (8s c0–4). Output keeps full bar r7, and paints the background suffix to the right of the shorter bars with 1: r3 c3–14 and r11 c5–14. Strong evidence for a rule involving completion/extension of shorter horizontal runs to a full-width reference line.
- Demo 3 (25x15, 0/6): output changes only r1 c10–14 and r8 c13–14 from 0 to 1. Those are trailing blank suffixes after the rightmost foreground in those rows. It leaves other rows unchanged, including a third bottom pair, so selection is conditional on some repeated-pattern/group relation, not simply every row with trailing background.
- Demo 2 (15x9, 0/2): top row `0 0 0 2 2 2 2 2 2`; output changes the 2-run c3–8 to 1. Other rows unchanged. Thus in some cases the selected suffix-like section is foreground instead of background; output color 1 is not a simple fixed background fill.
- Demo 4 (20x18, 4/9): output changes lower group r15 and r17 c13–17 to 1; in r16 it changes c13,c15,c17 (original 4) to 1, leaving the original 9s at c14,c16. This creates the same 3x5 pattern of 1s around preserved 9s. Upper group unchanged.
- Demo 5 (16x11, 5/2): two nearly identical 2-row patterns at r0–1 and r9–10. Output changes top r0 c9–10 from 5 to 1; rest unchanged. These are exactly locations where the top pattern differs from the lower copy (lower has 2s there).
- Demo 6 (16x20, 0/2): output changes top rows r0–2 c18–19 (zeros) to 1; rest unchanged. Lower group r6–8 retained. This is a 3x2 area where the top differs from lower (top zeros, lower 2s).

There may be one shared concept involving pattern continuation and marking the anomalous/missing portions. The test has two 4x22 bands (rows 6–9 and 21–24); it may require comparing aligned repeated pattern components/stripes or identifying rowwise continuation, but arbitrary painting of bottom/rightmost cells failed repeatedly.
